evidence: The prior price-only control retains trend participation but fails common-five and removed-leader economics. The path model has higher mean pre-2026 multiclass Brier error than a date-balanced historical-probability reference in all three pools; tail-specific rolling skill is positive on only136/88/128 of598 eligible dates. Common-five ranking alternatives are identical. Tail-warning price trajectories contain both missed reductions and profitable continuation; unconditional protective forecasts may hurt. This is not evidence that reliability gating will improve returns.

fixed_parent.ranking: Unchanged positive independent production price score. Forecast utility never ranks or grants an entry.
fixed_parent.holding: Use the independently written trend_book owner and its same-close broken-signal purchase veto. Config, RiskState, actual-unit/cash coordinator, order engine and all execution/cost assumptions stay unchanged.

forecast.reuse: Verified exact-universe issued arrays only, with their original generation identity. No model fitting, forecast slicing, training-source edits, or reference-strategy source code.

protective_authority: Where forecast authority is active, tail>=0.5 on a negative fresh return adds a full-exit warning. All current broken signals veto new units on that same close. The existing three-close recovery health predicate also requires tail<0.25 when that authority is active. Otherwise the existing independent price risk/admission rules apply. A model warning is a prediction, not a guaranteed loss. No absolute path-utility entry threshold is restored.
control: audit_tail=false grants the existing tail model this narrow risk role throughout. The model has no selection/ranking role. The current price-only study remains the separately source-bound baseline, not a newly hidden or retuned candidate.
audit: audit_tail=true grants that role only when strictly positive rolling tail Brier skill is observable. At close t, score only issued forecasts whose full20-session path has matured by t. Compare to the reference probability actually available at each issuance, not a reference fitted on later outcomes. Score each date equally across its valid quoted/ready names, then apply the existing120-session half-life over the latest120 issuance sessions. Require40 scored dates; no evidence or a zero reference-error denominator means no model authority. No p-value or statistical-certainty claim is made for this finite diagnostic.
reference: At each issuance construct Laplace-smoothed [-1,0,+1] outcome frequencies from complete labels only, using the same supplied pool, dates at least40, at most504 mature feature sessions and the inherited120-session half-life. Normalize contributions per date by the number of valid ready securities. The down-class probability is the tail reference; no future labels, current final-sample class frequencies or outside-pool data enter it.
state: The existing single actual-filled account remains the sole owner. Reliability changes never switch entire portfolios, cancel a latched exit or protective reduction, invent cash, reset account drawdown, forgive blocked orders, or rewrite legitimate historical decisions. It changes only prospective signal authority; price-based recovery and all mandatory risk latches remain. Each model-active warning and authority state must be traceable.
parameters: Exactly the two boolean candidates. Capacities, threshold0.5/0.25, horizon20, spans20/60, minimum40 scored dates, window120, half-life120 and training window504 are inherited reference/engine constants or the explicit fixed reliability design, not an optimization grid.
selection: Unchanged finite_study three-pool minimax incumbent wealth/drawdown/fill deficit, then objective/fills/tie-break, using only through2025-12-31. Record both candidates and exact predictions/reliability arrays. Evaluate the same selected candidate across unchanged full-period and retrospective2026 windows. Finite core improvement cannot replace original native-reference and robustness acceptance.
verification: new rule tests first fail before implementation
matured-label scoring and as-issued reference probabilities

non_goals: Do not expand rejected model/recovery grids, change old contracts/selector/metrics/costs/frozen data, promote failed evidence, use any four reference strategies as a source base, or claim calibrated probability scores imply economic acceptance.
